lastText: The Case Is ClosedNot ProvenNew Ending Discovered · 1 / 41THE PARK LANE TRIAL: THE COLONEL ACQUITTEDThe Crown has a name, a bullet and an arrest, and no witness who can say what was in the Colonel's hand. The jury is out for ninety minutes. When it comes in, the foreman, who is a draper, cannot bring himself to say the word, and says that the case is not proven. The Colonel bows to the judge, and goes out through the front door of the Old Bailey into a bright June noon. He ignores the gallery, in which you are sitting in a wig and a pair of spectacles. He has no need to look.
